answer: Selected paper from the most recent cs.CL listings: 'Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14483). Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability (MI) seeks mechanistic explanations for model behaviors, yet it lacks a formal framework for connecting mechanistic findings to behavioral claims. We propose that MI needs a logic of inference to bridge mechanistic facts and behavioral conclusions, and we introduce the Interpretability Calculus (IC) as a candidate formal system. IC uses syntax for causal interventions and feature quantification, and proof rules for deriving behavioral claims from mechanistic evidence. We demonstrate IC by formalizing a circuit analysis of induction heads, showing how mechanistic findings support a behavioral claim about next-token prediction. We argue that a logic of inference can help MI mature from descriptive case studies into a discipline capable of cumulative, auditable knowledge.
